18791. - TO THE PRINCE OF NEUCHATEL AND WAGRAM, 
MAJOR GENERAL OF THE GREAT ARMY, AT KOKNIGSRERG. 
Konigsberg, June 14, 1812. 


Cousin, it is time for you to think of organizing the rear of the army and taking your 
measures to make this organization complete. The hospitals, the stores, the post offices and even 
the police department are not organized anywhere. The commanders of weapons are not yet 
established. I have appointed a governor of old Prussia, who lives at Konigsberg. There must be 
local commanders at Pillau, Tapiau, Wehlau, Insterburg, Gurnbinnen, Stallupohnen, 
Wilkowyszki; there must be Elhing, Marienburg, Marienwerder, Bromberg, Thorn and Posen. 
The line of communication of the army at Konigsberg will be by Wilkowyszki, Insterhurg, and 
Wehlau. That of the army with France will be by Insterburg, Wehlau, Friedland, Gutlstadt, 
Oslerode, Thorn, Posen, Berlin, Magdeburg and Mainz. 

Reiterate your orders that no single man should pass the places of Thorn, Marienwerder, 
and Marienburg; but that they be united to be then sent to the army by marching companies of at 
least 100 men. Order the general of the artillery to have guns at Thorn, as well as at 
Marienwerder and Marienburg, in the works of the bridgeheads, in order to arm all the isolated 
men who would pass there, returning from the hospitals.**” 


489 


Page 490 


When the army has passed the Niemen, we will do the same thing: we will designate two 
or three points where all the men returning from the hospitals will have to be united, and from 
which they will leave only well armed and well dressed. 

Give me the state of the officers to be commanders of arms, and propose me the work of 
organization of the places. 

NAPOLEON.

My Cousin, I have ordered to establish at Konigsberg hospitals for 12,000 patients. Order 
the governor to have the necessary premises immediately chosen. Write to the Prince of 
Eckmiihl to have the premises necessary for the hospitals which I have ordered to establish at 
Gumbinnen and Stallupohnen for 1,000 men each; to the King of Naples, for those who will be 
established at Wilkowyszki, Wirballen, Kalwarya, and Mayampol; to the Duke of Reggio, for

1,000 patients, I will have on the Pregel and Alle hospitals for 24,000 sick or wounded. Defend 
accordingly any evacuation, without my order, lower than old Prussia.

18794. - TO THE PRINCE OF NEUCHATEL AND WAGRAM,

Konigsberg, June 15, 1812, 


My cousin, order the commander and the senior officer of the 17th Flotilla Crew 
Battalion, with all the sailors of this crew at Dunzig, to proceed without delay to Konigsberg. 
Only one company will remain for Danzig's service. A complete company of the same 17th 
battalion will be in charge of the defense of Pillau, it will have two small gunboats (which 
already exist) and three to four large canoes, the best walkers to be found at Konigsberg and 
Pillau, which will be armed as many oars as they can carry, and which will first be used to cross 
the tip of Nehruug Pillau, then sentinel on the pass and to be on any barge and other small 
buildings that would try to In the event that Pillau were attacked, that company, with 80 men, 
would serve the batteries, and another company of the same crew would do the same service at 
Memel, where there would be three small French gunboats, irrespective or 


491 


Page 492 


four or five Prussians who exist there. The other six companies of this crew will be employed 
until further notice, one with the Army Siege Engineer and Bridge crew, one with the 
Magdeburg Siege Crew, the remaining four will remain for navigation of the two lakes crews, 
Niemen and Pregel. It is useless to put five seamen per vessel; it is not even necessary to put in 
all; it suffices to have a certain number to correspond in a convoy, and to be able to; in case of 
event, bring them together to help a hand. The 4th battalion of the flotilla will be entirely united 
for the passage of the bridges. 

The battalion of the Scheldt will be divided in two; two companies will remain at Danzig, 
and two will be attached to the workshops at Konigsberg. Accordingly, you will order that two of 
the companies which are at Danzig, wheelwrights and others, leave without delay to go to 
Konigsberg.

Prussian artillery company, 100 men; finally, a company of Prussian invalids, 100 men; so that 
he will have altogether 2,500 men.

18799. - TO EUGENE NAPOLEON, VICE-KING OF ITALY, 
COMMANDING THE 4th AND 6th CORPS OF THE GREAT ARMY IN RASTENBURG. 
Konigsberg. June 15, 1812. 


My Son, you will be ordered to take your headquarters on the 20th to Oletzko and be 
there with your army corps, to place the Bavarians at Lyk and the 3rd Cavalry Corps near Seyny. 
The King of Westphalia will have, on the 30th, his headquarters at Nowogrod. The Duke of 
Elchingen will be at Kalwarya; the prince of Echmihl, to Wilkowyszki; the Duke of Reggio at 
Gumbinnen; the Guard, after the 1st body. My headquarters will probably be in Wilkowyszki or 
Stallupcehnen. The Duke of Tarentum will be at Tilsit, in a position opposite Georgusburg, at 
which time the Austrian corps of Prince Schwarzenberg will be at Lublin, and this will be 
necessary to judge the movements.I calculate that the Russian general Wittgenstein will be 
detained with his three divisions opposite Georgenburg, Tilsit and Memel, and an embarkation 
by the Haff to threaten him, that the other four divisions of the army of Tolly, with the Imperial 
Guard, will be on Rovno and Olitta, that General Essen, with his four divisions, could be 
between Grodno and Meretch, General Bagration on Brzesc and Bialrstok, and in that situation 
my intention is to go between Kovno and Olitta. bridges at once and pass with the Ist, 2nd, 3rd 
Corps and the Guard, and even with the 4th and 6th Corps, quickly emerging on Vilna. In this 
assumption the King of Westphalia would push quickly from Nowogrod on Bialystok to follow 
Bagration: I expect that the first shots will be fired on the 22nd or the 23rd, on the Kovno side. 
As I will be at my Gumbinnen headquarters on the 18th and 19th, I will send you my orders for 
subsequent movements. I will direct you to Kalwarya or Seyny, depending on the circumstances. 
The 6th corps must always support you. The*”® 





496 


Page 497 


passage once done, if the enemy abandoned the river, I suppose you have boats with you; you 
have pontoons and sailors, and you could easily throw a bridge about sixty toises; which could 
shorten you even a walk and you would not have to come over the bridges that I would have 
thrown away. You must also find some means of passage in the country. How many boats do 
you have? It is fitting that you instruct General Saint-Cyr in my plans, that you have an eye on 
what the enemy does on the side of Grodno; that you are in great, safe and rapid communication 
with Prince Poniatowski, and that you do not rely on the post for this, but that it is by the means 
of pickets of cavalry, whose horses serve to the officers in dispatch, that the correspondence can 
take place. 

I do not need to recommend secrecy to you about these provisions. 

Rally all your troops, especially your French troops. If you have cartridges on your rear, 
have them move forward to serve as replacements. Continue to supply Willenberg, if possible, 
unless your convoys can come to the camp. I suppose you will leave Rastenburg with your 
twenty days of food, since I have 900,000 rations at your disposal. However, if what I have given 
you is not enough, I would not mind to give you another 10,000 quintals of flour at Wehlau, 
provided you could send them to take them. When leaving Rasteuburg, form a hospital there, let 
a very good commander of the place and a detachment of cavalry and gendarmerie. Make sure 
the post remains organized. Independently of the commander, leave an officer there who has 
your confidence and who can direct all the couriers of Warsaw and from the right on the place 
where I will be. 

NAPOLEON.

18800. - TO JEROME NAPOLEON, KING OF WESTPHALIA, 
COMMANDING THE 5th, 7th AND 8th CORPS OF THE GREAT ARMY, AT WARSAW 
Konigsberg, June 15, 1812. 


My Brother, the Major General, has made known to you your orders, according to which 
you must have your headquarters on the 20th at Nowowod, the Viceroy at Olelzko, and the 
Bavarians at Lyk. Everything leads me to think that the first shots will take place from the 22nd 
to the 23rd.*°” 





497 


Page 498 


The Russian corps of the Left can hardly be informed until the 24th or the 25th. I have nothing to 
add to the general instructions which I have given you, nor in case the enemy should take the 
offensive; it seems to me that everything has been planned, and that in this case my intentions 
have been well explained to you. 

I am taking my headquarters to Wehlau tomorrow, after to Insterburg, and the 18th to 
Gumbinnen. Send me your dispatches by Rastenburg. I order the viceroy to leave there an 
intelligent place commander and a little gendarmerie. The local commander will direct the mails. 
As soon as I have passed the Niemen, I may resolve to walk on Vilna. Then I will lend the flank 
to Bagration's army. It will be necessary for you to follow it closely so that you can take part in 
the movement that I will make against this army. If I could separate it from the rest of the 
Russian troops and fall on its right flank, you would have to be able to attack it at the same time 
as I attack it. 

I have seen two battalions of your brigades, which seemed to me very well; I put them 
online because I thought it was the best way to bring them closer to you. As soon as I can meet, I 
will put them back in your corps. 

The news of the peace of the Turks with Russia is countered. I received letters from 
Bucharest on the 28th, and peace was not made. 

Always make the noise that I come to Warsaw. Do not touch your twenty days of food. 
You must only touch it in the presence of the enemy. There is a great deal of complaint about the 
discipline of your troops: it is said that everyone is doing what he wants. Hold Reynier and 
Vandamme. 

If you arrive on Bialystok and Grodno, it will be convenient to organize the country. You 
will charge Prince Poniatowski with this care. He will put Poles in it. Here you will find 
considerable resources. 

The Saxons have with them a crew of pontoons; bring these pontoons to you on the spot; 
I see that the Poles have some too; it will be precious to you; the Saxons, coming behind, do not 
need it. I have already asked you about the number of pontoons you have. 

NAPOLEON.

18801. - TO MARSHAL DAVOUT, PRINCE OF ECKMUHL, 
COMMANDING THE Ist CORPS OF THE GREAT ARMY, AT GUMBINNEN. 
Konigsberg, June 15, 1812. 


My Cousin, the Major General, sends you an order of movement according to which your 
corps must be united at Milkowyszki on the 20th. From Gumbinnen there are only two marches; 
leaving on the 19th, you will be the 20th at Wilkowyszki. The two battalions of the 25th join you 
and pass today to Konigsberg. I ordered that there should not be a single man of the 111th 
tomorrow in Konigsberg. The 4th and 6th Battalions of the 25th left Danzig; that of the 61st also 
left Pillau. A detachment of 200 men from the 25th, whom you had left near Elbing, was ordered 
to join. It is likely that from the 22nd to the 23rd we will fight, and that it will be two steps 
further than Wilkowyszki. It is therefore fitting for you to gather your detachments as soon as 
possible, and especially your French troops. You have for your escorts the troops of 
Mecklenburg and the other German troops; you can not give these chores to the French troops 
and spare them. It seems to me that you do not follow this system enough, which is important. 
As you are enlightened by the cavalry of the 1st Reserve Corps on the directions of Kovno and 
Olitta, place your light cavalry on the direction of Georgenburg, between the Niemen and you. 
Have staff officers on the Georgenburg side and elsewhere, who promptly instruct you of the 
offensive movement that the enemy would make, Consult your situation reports, and recall all 
your detachments. As soon as the carriages which are sent to you from Konigsberg, and which 
bring you 10 to 12,000 quintals of flour to Gumbinnen, will have arrived, I think it would be 
proper that after their unloading you return them at once to Insterburg for to recharge there, and 
then what they bring from Insterburg would take you to your Wilkowyszki camp. 

NAPOLEON. 

From the original comm. by the Marechal Princess Eckmithl.

18803. - TO COMTE BIGOT DE PHEAMENEU, 
MINISTER OF REGLION, IN PARIS. 
Konigsberg, June 16, 1812. 


Count Bigot de Préameneu, I receive your report of June 5th. The priests, being subject 
like the others, are subject to the same oath. But we must distinguish: there is the ecclesiastical 
oath, which has been prescribed by the Concordat; the only penalty I impose on the priest who 
does not wish to lend him is the pearl of the ecclesiastical benefit he enjoys. But the oath of 
obedience to the Constitutions of the Empire and loyalty to the Emperor is due by all the 
citizens; those who refuse to lend him the penalty of my decree. Write, then, to the bishop, and 
make these unfortunate people understand how this refusal would be contrary to their duties. 
When they have taken this last oath, they will only come out of exile. In order for them to be 
able to return to their profits, they must take the oath of the Condordat.

18806. - TO GENERAL CLARKE, DUKE OF FELTRE, 
MINISTER OF WAR, IN PARIS. 
Konigsberg, June 16, 1812. 


Duke de Feltre, all the executives who make up the Lagrange division will soon have 
joined. It is necessary to return from Spain all the useless frameworks. There are, I believe, in the 
interior a good number of frames that are not full. Make me a report on all this. 

Cohort formation is not progressing; you have not yet sent me any state officers to 
confirm, 

I think I have told you that it was proper to send the demi-brigades who were at 
Cherbourg to Bayonne. It is about 4,000 men who will be useful at Bayonne, and whose 
departure will relieve Normandy in terms of consumption. If the circumstances of Spain became 
urgent, you could still, without waiting for my orders, also direct the demi-brigade of Pontivy to 
Bayonne. You see that it would give Bayonne a very considerable mass of forces, since it would 
bring together two cohorts, four demi-brigades forming, I believe, sixteen battalions, and five or 
six battalions of the Bayonne reserve; that would make a total of 22 to 24 battalions or 15 to 
18,000 men; reserve that would put in the case, especially after the summer, to effectively rescue 
the North. 

I recommend you to pay special attention to all the cavalry depots of the Spanish army, in 
order to draw from 3 to 4,000 horses, which would be added to this reserve. 

Also send the 10th, 11th and 12th brigades to Berlin; they are very useless in France, and 
nothing leads one to think that the English can attempt anything.” au

18812. - TO THE PRINCE OF NEUCHATEL AND WAGRAM, 
MAJOR GENERAL OF THE GREAT ARMY, IN KOENGSBERG. 
Konigsberg, June 16, 1812 


Cousin, the roads of the army between the Vistula and Niemen will be as follows: Thorn 
will be taken for two days to Graudenz; the Prussian commander of Graudenz will supply food 
for a day to Marienwerder; at Marienwerder, supplies for a day to Marienburg, there, provisions 
for a day to Elhing; at Elbing the provisions for three days will be taken to Konigsberg: to 
Konigsberg, stay; we will take the food for a day to Tapiau; at Tapiau, provisions for two days to 
Gumbinnen; in Gumbinnen, two days of food up to Wilkowyszki. Thus the troops will be twelve 
days en route from Thorn to Gumbinnen, including the stay of Konigsberg, they will take a stay 
at Gumbinnen. It will be thirteen days. All intermediate routes will be deleted; however, a 
command with a Prussian garrison, a store-keeper, and a handling department will be kept at 
Osterode, and 10,000 quintals of flour will be maintained there. There will be a similar 
establishment in Rastenburg. 

The communication of the army with Warsaw will be as follows: two days of food will 
be taken at Warsaw to Pultusk; in Pultusk.>”* 





504 


Page 505 


three days of food up to Willenberg; at Willenberg, three days of food up to Rastenburg, where 
three days of food will be taken to Gumbinnen. There will be French commanders, handlers and 
flour stores in Willenberg and Pultusk. 

The communication of Danzig with the army will be made either by Pillau or by 
Marienburg: by Pillau, they will take food for three days at Danzig as far as Pillau; at Pillau, 
provisions for two days to Konigsberg, & c. If the route is made by Marienburg, we will take 
food for two days at Danzig, to Marienburg, whence we will follow the line. 

The communication of Konigsberg to Tilsit will be made by taking Konigsberg drunk for 
a day to Tapiau; at Tapiau, one day of food up to Loebau, where two days of food will be 
provided to Tilsit. 

Thus it is necessary to Thorn a commander of place: he exists there; Marienwerder must 
be a commander and a handler: there are some at Marienburg, Elbing, Konigsberg, Tapiau, and 
Insterburg. A commander is needed at Osterode and Willenberg; there is one at Pultusk; you 
need one in Rastenburg. All other commanders and commissioners of war must be recalled. 

Care must be taken to place French employees in the hospitals to be established, and to 
order them to correspond with General Latour at Elbing and with General Hogendorp at 
Konigsberg for Old Prussia. 

You will order that the roads from Marienwerdcr to Marienburg and Elbing and from 
Marienburg to Dirschau be mended and maintained.

From the original. Deposit of the war.

18817. - ORDER. 
Insterburg, June 17, 1812. 


The Bromberg Canal and the navigation of the Netze and Warta will be in the best 
condition. 

A commission, composed of an engineer officer to be appointed by the director of 
Danzig, of Senft Senft, advisor to the regency of the New March, and of an engineer to be 
appointed by the Minister of the Interior of the Duchy of Warsaw, will meet on the 25th of this 
month in Bromberg. 

This commission will determine all the work to be done temporarily, without interrupting 
navigation. 

It will remove the piles that obstruct the passages and build the necessary locks, either 
stone or wood.” 


507 


Page 508 


A sum of 100,000 francs, which will be charged to the reserve funds of the Grand Army 
set at 3 million by the budget of 28 May, will be placed at the disposal of the said commission to 
be employed, without waiting for another authorization, the work which will be judged the most 
urgent. 

During the month of July, the commission will send us a report on the system of work 
which it will propose to accelerate this navigation, and the estimate of the expenditure which will 
result from it. 

The Intendant General and the Commander-in-Chief of the Army Engineers are 
responsible for the execution of this order. 

NAPOLEON. 

From the original, Depot of War.

My Son, Prescription Officer Tascher handed me your letter. Delay your movement until

convoy of the wagons that you sent, which happens to you. You must also receive the convoy of

the headquarters forming a consumption of 20,000 rations, it will require 160,000 rations for

the small headquarters will resume their 200 quintals of flour and will be ready to leave at ten

18831. - ORDERS 
FOR JEROME NAPOLEON, KING OF WESTPHALIA, 
COMMANDING THE 5th, 7th AND 8th CORPS OF THE GREAT ARMY, AT PULTUSK. 
Gumbinnen, June 20, 1812. 


The Emperor orders that the 5th corps starts on the 22nd to be the 25th at Augustowo; 
that the 8th starts on the 23rd to go on Raygrod; that these two corps have with them their twenty 
days of food. The 4th Cavalry Corps will cover these two corps on the Bialystok and Grodno 
Road, and will push its posts on both directions. 

The 6th corps will be at Suwalki on the 23rd, and the viceroy's headquarters will be the 
same day in Kaluarya. The deck crew belonging to the corps will walk with the 5th. 

The 7th corps, which will arrive on the 21st or 22nd at Siedlce, will march on the 23rd on 
Brok, leaving an infantry brigade, with cavalry and artillery, at Siedke, until the Austrian corps 
which must arrive on the 25th, On the 24th, as soon as it is certain that the enemy can no longer 
obstruct the arrival of the Austrians at Siedlce, this brigade will join Brok with his division. 

The 8th corps will be weakened by a regiment left to Modlin and another left to Praga. If, 
in the interval between the 22nd and the 25th, the enemy advances to Warsaw, the brigade which 
will be in Siedlce will be on Praga el Sierock, and the corps which will be in Brok will be on 
Pullusk and Oslrolenka; but this hypothesis is unlikely. General Reynier will still be responsible 
for covering Warsaw, Praga and Modlin. 

On the 24th and the 25th, when the army will take the offensive, the Austrians being in 
position at Siedlce, if the enemy has not attempted anything offensive, the king of Westphalia 
will be able to order the 7th corps to approach of Bialystok and Grodno, supposing that the 
march of the King and the movements of the army accelerate the movement of the enemy on 
Vilna. 

NAPOLEON. 


According to the original. Deposit of the war.

proper harm, bearing in mind, however, that his The main purpose must be to cover Warsaw and 
Modlin, that it is to be hoped that on the 26th he will be informed of what will have happened at 
Kovno on the 24th and 25th; which will give light on the situation of the enemy, and will enable

18839. - TO MARSHAL DAVOUT, PRINCE OF ECKMUHL, 
COMMANDING THE Ist CORPS OF THE GREAT ARMY, IN WILKOWYSZKI. 
Gumbinnen, June 20, 1812, eight o'clock in the evening, 


Cousin, I receive your different letters. I put General Subervie and the Wiirttemberg 
General on the agenda. I suppressed the Wurtemberg brigade and put it to the order of the army, 
that is to say of Europe, I flew to write to the royal prince that he ran the risk of having the 
greater inconvenience if he did not order it; but on your side try to stop one of the looters, to send 
him to the provost of the army, who will shoot him. 

You will see by the orders I have given that I want the crews to pass in a straight line by 
the Kovno road (by the Skraudze road). I detach a crew of 60 toises on Maryampol. I need to 
make my main visit to Kovno, because of the intersection of the two rivers and the greater 
proximity of Tilsit, from where I have to pull my supplies; but the army is so great, that I will 
make a bridge to Preuy, where I will send the Duke of Elchingen and the Viceroy. The crew 
from elsewhere can from everywhere’ 


519 


Page 520 


go to Preny; from Skraudze he can go to Preny; even if it is lower, it can still go. It is necessary 
therefore that this crew passes on the road of Skraudze; but it is very important that the crew and 
the troops are not seen. You must not occupy Maryampol, where the Duke of Elchingen's corps 
is placed. Do not go to Zapiecyszki either, because the way is impracticable and will unmask all 
our movements. Be careful not to show any infantrymen or cuirassiers. The first infantryman to 
be seen by the enemy must be a pontoonist. Leave your bakers at Wilkowyszki's ovens to cook 
every day of the 21st and 22nd on your behalf, unless you have biscuit. I reduced the Guard's 
ration to 12 ounces of bread, 5 ounces of flour, and 1 ounce of rice; by this means we save a lot 
of bread. He has passed here since yesterday carts that carry you more than 4 to 5,000 quintals of 
flour for you. 

NAPOLEON. 

From the original comm. by the Marechal Princess Eckmiihl. 


18840. - ORDER OF THE DAY. 
Gumbinnen. June 20, 1812. 


The Guard will take in the day for six days of bread that the soldiers will carry on them. 
The ration will consist of the following: 12 ounces of bread, 5 ounces of flour, 1 ounce of rice. 
These provisions will be for the 20th, 21st, 22nd, 23rd, 24th and 25th. 

Six more days of food will be distributed to the Guard tomorrow. The regiments will 
leave for this purpose pickets and cars per battalion to carry them. 

The bakers will stay today and tomorrow 21 in Gumbinnen to make bread. The Guard 
will have food for the 26th, 27th, 28th, 29th, 30th and Ist of July. 

It is recommended that the soldiers spare their food and take care of it. The officers will 
make inspections every morning to make sure that every soldier has only eaten the food day he 
owes, and that he has the rest for the number of days he wants. 

NAPOLEON. 

From the original. Deposit of the war. 


18841. lst BULLETIN OF THE GREAT ARMY (1). 
Gumbinnen. June 20, 1812. 


At the end of 1810, Russia changed its political system: the English spirit 





1) Not all the Bulletins of the Grand Army will be found below.*” 


520 


Page 521 


regained his influence; the ukase on commerce was the first act. 

In February 1811, five divisions of the Russian army left the Danube on forced marches 
and went to Poland. By this movement, Russia sacrificed Wallachia and Moldavia. 

The Russian armies assembled and formed, a protest was made against France, which 
was sent to all the cabinets. Russia announced that she did not even want to keep appearances. 

All means of conciliation were employed on the part of France; all was useless. 

At the end of 1811, six months later, we saw in France that all this could only end in war; 
we prepared for it. 

The garrison of Danzig was increased to 20,000 men. Supplies of all kinds, guns, rifles, 
powder, ammunition, and deck-crews, were directed to that place; considerable sums were 
placed at the disposal of the engineers to increase the fortifications. The army was put on the war 
foot. The cavalry, the artillery train and the military crews were completed. 

In March, 1812, a treaty of alliance was concluded with Austria; the previous month a 
treaty had been concluded with Prussia. 

In April, the 1st Corps of the Grand Army moved on the Oder; the 2nd corps went to the 
Elbe; the 3rd corps on the lower Oder; the 4th corps left Verona, crossed the Tyrol, and went to 
Silesia. 

The Guard left Paris. 

On the 22nd of April, the Emperor of Russia took the command of his army, left 
Petersburg, and carried his headquarters to Vilna. 

At the beginning of May the Ist corps reached the Vistula, Elbing, and Marienburg; the 
2nd corps, at Marienwerder; the 3rd corps, at Thorn; 4th and 6th corps at Plock; the 5th corps 
meets in Warsaw; the 8th corps, on the right of Warsaw; the 7th corps, in Pulawi, 

The Emperor left St. Cloud on May 9, crossed the Rhine on the 13th, the Elbe on the 
29th, and the Vistula on the 6th of June.

18842. - TO GENERAL CLARKE, DUKE OF FELTRE, 
MINISTER OF WAR, IN PARIS. 
Gumbinnen, June 21, 1812. 


Duke de Feltre, I receive your letter of June 11, which reports the arrival of six cohorts of 
National Guard at Cherbourg. That being the case, I think that it is proper to direct the two demi- 
brigades which were destined to the guard of Cherbourg on Bayonne, to increase the reserve; for 
I attach great importance to having there a considerable force that can remedy what can be done 
in the North. Let me know what will happen in the course of July, the situation of the Bayonne 
reserve. 

Direct the 3rd battalions of the 127th and 128th on Berlin, by the road which distances 
them more from the 32nd military division; but do not send these soldiers until they are already a 
little disciplined. 

NAPOLEON.

18849. - TO EUGENE NAPOLEON, VICE-KING OF ITALY, 
COMMANDING THE 4th AND 6th CORPS OF THE GREAT ARMY, IN OLETZKO. 
Gumbinnen, June 21, 1812. 


My Son, you have received orders from the Major General to return to Kulwarya as soon 
as possible. The 3rd Corps Cavalry is ordered to marry Maryampol. The cavalry of your corps 
will serve to enlighten you on Meretch and Olitta. If it is possible, it will be the 24th between 
Maryampol and Preny, in order to cross the bridge that the Duke of Elchingen will establish. 

I ordered the king of Westphalia to carry with the 5th and 8th corps on Augustowo, and 
to march from there on Grodno. 

Hostilities will begin on the 24th. I will cross the river at Kovno. 

Probably I will send the Duke of Elchingen from Kovno to Preny. You will try to be 
ready with your army corps to pass on the bridge. General Reynier is under observation at Brok; 
the Austrians are in Siedlce to cover Warsaw. 

Do you keep in touch with the King of Westphalia? to which I gave orders to press on the 
left and take the line of operation on Konigsberg, in case the enemy should come to his right. 

I will be tonight at Wilkowyszki, and on the 23rd near Kovno. Prepare all your means of 
passage. 

NAPOLEON

18850. - TO JEROME NAPOLEON, KING OF WESTPHALIA, 
COMMANDING THE 5th, 7th, AND 8th CORPS OF THE GREAT ARMY AT NOWOGROD. 
Gumbinnen, June 21, 1812. 


Brother, you will have received orders from the General Staff to take up position on 
Augustowo, and for General Reynier to be in observation corps on Brok or Oslrow. 

The Austrians will, it seems, be on the 23rd or the 24th at Siedlce. General Reynier must 
always aim to cover Warsaw, Pultusk and Ostrolenka. 

You have to press the center. In case the enemy turns your right, or even the line of 
operation will be on Konigsberg, Tachs that the Poles arrive on the 23rd at Augustowo, and have 
an advanced guard on Grodno with many light troops. Advance your bridge in this direction. It is 
probable that I will give you the order to carry you on Grodno with all your army, putting by this 
movement on your rear what is at Bialystok. This” 


525 


Page 526 


movement would evacuate all this province. You will be in continuity with the army, so that 
everything will always give in mass, and one will then operate against General Bagration, 
according to the position which it will occupy. 

Maintain the greatest order, prevent waste. It is complained that the Westphalian officers 
were fed in Warsaw; it's worthless, especially for people who approach you. 

Stand in correspondence with the viceroy on your left. 

General Reynier will be able to reach Bialystok, as soon as you arrive at Grodno, always 
having for principal instruction to cover Warsaw. 

The Austrians will stand in observation against the body of Bagration. 

I have several times sent you to advance the pontoons which the Saxons have on the 
vanguard of the corps. Have your sappers, etc., run there, so that the passage can be made very 
quickly. 

NAPOLEON. 

I'll be at Wilkowsszki tonight.

the Ist, 2nd, 3rd corps, the Guard and the cavalry, to publish it only on the 21st at daybreak.

Division, and that, as to the Prussian corps, he should not communicate it to them, but that he 
should make them one to his will, in which he will say in a few words that the war has begun and 
that Russia wants it. Write to the King of Westphalia to make it known to the 5th 7th and 8th 
Corps, only in the morning of the 26th. Send the proclamation to Prince Schwnrzenberg, and, as 
it is not suitable for his army corps, instruct him to substitute for it the one that suits him, only by 
making known that the war has begun. He will publish this communication on the 26th. 
Communicate my proclamation to the viceroy; he will give it to his corps and to the Bavarians 
on the 25th. The governors of Konigsberg and Danzig will publish it on the 27th. Send it, by the 
courier of this day, to my ministers at Vienna and Berlin; send it also to my minister at Warsaw. 
They will have it published only on the 26th. Thus this proclamation will be for the whole army, 
with the exception of the Austrians and Prussians, to whom the commanders of these corps will 
make particular proclamations.

18855. - PROCLAMATION TO THE BIG ARMY. 
Imperial district of Wilkowyszki. June 22, 1812. 


Soldiers! the second war of Poland is begun; the first ended at Friedland and Tilsit. At 
Tilsit Russia swore eternal alliance to France and war to England. She is violating her oaths 
today! She will give no explanation of her strange conduct, which the French eagles have passed 
over the Rhine, thus leaving our allies at her discretion. Russia is driven by fate; his destinies 
must be fulfilled. Would she believe us degenerate? Are we no longer the soldiers of Austerlitz? 
It places us between dishonor and war: the choice: can not be doubtful. So let's go ahead: let's 
move the Niemen, let's take the>”® 





528 


Page 529 


war on its territory. The second war of Poland will be glorious to French arms, as the first. But 
the peace which we shall conclude will carry with it its guarantee and put an end to the fatal 
influence which Russia has exercised for fifty years on the affairs of Europe. 
NAPOLEON. 
From the original. Deposit of the war. 


18856. - ORDER FOR THE ARMY. 
Imperial District of Wilkowyszki, June 22, 1812. 


TITLE 1. 


The Emperor orders the marshals and generals commanding the army corps, the generals 
commanding divisions and brigades, and the corps commanders to take all necessary measures to 
keep the army in the greatest order and to prevent disorder who are starting to desolate the 
country, accordingly: 

1. Every marshal or general commanding a corps d'armee shall appoint a provostal 
commission composed of five officers, before which shall be brought any soldier who, after the 
army, has been absent from his regiment without any legitimate cause, any marauder, Anyone 
who is caught is either plundering or molesting the inhabitants of the country. This commission 
will condemn the culprits to death and have them executed within twenty-four hours. 

2. There will be established at Maryampol, for the department of Lomza, a provostal 
commission of five officers, with whom will be formed a mobile column, composed of 200 
inhabitants of the country (national guard), 10 gendarmes and 40 men of French cavalry. This 
column will be commanded by a general or superior officer, French. It will be subdivided into 
ten small columns or patrols, each of twenty-five men, who will cross the country in all 
directions and stop any straggler or marauder and any troublemaker. Arrested individuals shall 
be brought before the Maryampol Provost Committee and, if guilty, sentenced in accordance 
with the above. 

3. There will be a Provostal Commission for the province of Konigsberg, which will sit at 
Konigsberg; it will be composed of five officers and organized by the governor of Konigsberg. A 
mobile column consisting of 100 men of Prussian cavalry, 200 men of Prussian infantry, 10 
French gendarmes and 40 men of cavalry and infantry will be formed under this French 
committee.” 


529 


Page 530 


This movable column will be divided into ten small columns, which will traverse the country in 
all directions, arrest the marauders and laggards, all the individuals informed of crimes, and 
translate them to Konigsberg before the provost commission. 

4. A Provost Committee will be established in Warsaw under the orders of General 
Dutaillis, Governor of Warsaw, who will be responsible for its organization. 300 men of Polish 
troops in the Grand Duchy and 10 gendarmes will form the mobile column, which will be 
divided into ten small columns charged with covering the departments of Warsaw, Kalisz, 
Krakow, Lublin, and Siedlce. The National Guard will lend them everywhere a hand, and any 
traitor, marauder, etc., will be arrested and judged by the Warsaw Provost Marshal. 

5. There will be such a commission in Posen, 300 men of the National Guard, of the 
Polish cavalry, 10 French gendarmes and 20 men from the depots will form the mobile column, 
which will be divided into 10 small columns, to traverse the departments of Posen and Bromberg 
and stop all the marauders. 

6. There will be a provost commission in Danzig. The governor will supply ten small 
columns of 30 men each, to cross Pomerania to the Oder, stop all the stragglers and marauders 
and bring them before the provost commission. 

7. There will be a provost commission at Elbing, for the province of Marienwerder. 10 
French gendarmes and 50 Prussian cavalrymen will form the mobile column, which will be 
divided into five patrols or small columns, which will be constantly moving. 

8. There will be formed at Berlin such a provostal commission under the governor, who 
will organize as many small columns as it will be necessary to put the police between the Oder 
and the Elbe. 


TITLE I. 


9. It is expressly forbidden for the commanders of the various posts and passages on the 
Oder and on the Vistula, notably those of Warsaw, Plock, Thorn, Graudenz, Maricnwerder, 
Marienburg and Elbing, to let pass no isolated soldier. Isolated men, coming out of hospitals, 
convalescents, or absent from their corps' under any pretext whatsoever, will be retained by the 
commanders of Glogau, Kiistrin and Stettin, until these commanders have been able to gather 
100 well armed and well dressed to form a company which they will direct on the places of the 
Vistula. 


10. The commanders of the place on the Vistula will also retain’? 


530 


Page 531 


leave the isolated men alone until they have been able to gather 100 men whom they can train in 
company of march and to direct on Konigsberg. 

11. The commanders of Konigsberg, Wehlau, Insterburg, and Gumbinnen will prevent 
the movement of all isolated men, and will detain all men from intermediate hospitals, until they 
can form companies of 100 men, well armed, and state to join; they will then direct them to 
Kovno. 

12. Place commanders, hospital directors, commissioners of wars giving road-cards and 
storekeepers supplying food to isolated men shall be responsible for the non-execution of this 
measure. 

War commissioners, hospital directors and storekeepers will receive instructions from the 
Intendant General in this regard. 

13. The movable columns will stop all individuals in contravention of the present order, 
and direct them to the nearest place. 

14. The present order will be printed, read to the order of all the bodies, put in the order 
of all the places and posted on the doors of all the hospitals, all the bailiffs and all the town halls 
of the communes .

18857. - ORDER FOR THE PASSAGE OF THE NIEMEN. 
Imperial Camp Nauaardyszki, June 23, 1812. 


The Prince of Eckmihl will be in charge of setting the bridges, of controlling the passage, 
and of passing the first with his army corps. General Eble will be under his command, with all 
the deck crew, the engineering parks, the workmen and sailors attached to him. 

At eight o'clock in the evening, the deck crew will set in motion, namely: Major-General 
Morand, at the head of three companies of voltigeurs of the 13th light infantry, commanded by a 
battalion commander of choice, 50 sappers and a captain of engineers. Each sapper will have his 
tool. Each outfielder will have a tool on his bag. In addition, packets of cartridges will be 
distributed, so that each outfielder or sapper has sixty cartridges at the time of passage. 

General Eble will divide his bridge into four parts, with the intention of throwing four 
bridges. One or two bridge companies will be sold at each bridge; it will be attached to them 
too 





53 


Page 532 


one or two companies of sappers, one or two companies of workmen, one or two companies of 
sailors, under the orders of a superior officer of pontonniers. Seamen and engineers, whatever 
their rank, will be subordinated to the pontoon officers. 

One of the bridges will be thrown opposite the hillock, to the left of the Jesia; the other 
two, between this one and the village of Poniemon, so that there will be at least 150 fathoms 
from one bridge to the other; at ten o'clock in the evening, the three decks having arrived in front 
of their site and in the greatest silence, the boats will be launched. The 300 men will be thrown to 
the other side; no fire will be fired unless absolutely necessary. The battalion commander will 
barricade his 300 men in the village by making cuts. 

General Pernety will at the same time place the 2nd Corps reserve batteries on the hill. 

The reserve battery. The 2nd corps will start at six o'clock to approach Poniemon and be 
carried on the right, in the place which will be recognized as the most favorable beyond the 
island. 

A company of the 4th Battalion of the 13th Light Infantry will be thrown into the island 
which is opposite Poniemon. 

The light battery and the foot battery of the Morand division will be placed, the battery 
on horseback, on the left of the Jesia, between the nipple and the mouth of the Jesia; the battery 
on foot, four pieces within range of the second bridge and four pieces on the right of the third 
bridge. 

The four mounted horse batteries of the corps will remain with their division. 

The four foot batteries will be placed in the village of Poniemon and distributed in four 
batteries, between the reserve battery and the last bridge. The battery of the 2nd division will be 
the first; that of the third will be the second; that of the 4th, the third 1 and that of the 5th will be 
the fourth. Each battery to pass with his division, it will be a pure movement to the left. 

The corps will take up arms at seven o'clock. 

We will make sure that the soldiers have eaten the soup. We will inspect the bags and 
cartridges, and we will ensure that they have with them for four days of food, without the 
luggage and caissons, nothing to pass. 

At eight o'clock the corps will set out and move between Alexota and Jesia on sixteen 
leagues, each regiment forming a line at the distance of half a battalion, the colonel and the 
regimental staff placed before the eagle of the Ist battalion; Brigadier General?** 





532 


Page 533 


forward, in the center of his brigade, the regimental pieces to the right of each line, and 
constantly harnessed, with all the caissons and ambulances of the regiments; the general of 
division behind the center of the 3rd line, with the commissaries of wars, administrations and 
ambulances of the division; the battery on horseback on the left of the division. 

There will be, from one division to another, the distance of half a battalion. The divisions 
will be in order of numbers. 

The brigade of light cavalry on two lines, each regiment forming a line, having the 
brigadier-general at its head, the horses saddled, but unbridled. 

All the officers of the staff of the army corps, between the Ist and the 2nd division, with 
the commissioners of wars, officers of the engineers, etc. 

The sapper companies will be at their division; they will be with the batteries on 
horseback, all the caissons of cartridges, the artillery park of the three divisions and the caissons 
of tools, so that at ten o'clock everything is thus in position. 

The 13th light infantry will be in battle beside the pontonniers, where is the general 
Morand, in order to be used, according to the circumstances, to reinforce the men on the right 
bank, or for any other service. 

At ten o'clock in the evening the three bridges must be thrown away. Morand's division 
will result in three columns, that is to say, by brigade, each brigade having at its head the 
regimental pieces. The divisional general will pass by the bridge of the center. The light artillery 
battery will pass by the left bridge, that is to say by the one situated before the mouth of the 
Jesia, at the tail of the brigade which passes on this bridge. The foot battery will go halfway to 
the right bridge and half to the center bridge. 

General Pajol will pass with the two elite companies of his brigade, one at the center 
bridge and the other at the right bridge. 

The past division will take a position which supports its right and left at the Niemen (1), 
its artillery in position, and will thus wait for the day. She will be able to carry 1,000 fathoms 
forward, always leaving the three companies of voltigeurs in the village and in the shelter. 

The cavalry will not make a patrol; it will only remain in the form of a grand guard, a 
company in the direction of Kovno, and the other in the direction of the rising river; everyone 
under arms and on horseback.

In this state of things, the Prince of Eckmihl will take my orders for the time when the

As soon as the town is occupied, the fourth bridge will be thrown in the ordinary passage

parts will remain coupled. 

As soon as each division is formed, the men will dismount; they will settle at the bivouac; 
the horses will be saddled, but unbridled.

18859. - TO THE PRINCE OF NEUCHATEL AND WAGRAM, 
MAJOR GENERAL OF THE GREAT ARMY, IN KOVNO. 
Kovno. June 24, 1812. 


My Cousin, a small cavalry depot will be formed at Kovno. 

Order the King of Naples to send his men and horses back to this little depot and appoint 
an officer to command him. Recommend that you lighten as much as you can. Be sure to attach a 
geographer engineer who sends a sketch of the country's situation twice a day. Ask this engineer 
for information on the Strava River, its width, depth and height. As soon as the cavalry has 
passed Jijmory, it is necessary that he sends strong brigades of light cavalry to light on the 
outlets of Olitta, because, if Iam well informed on all that happens on this road, he could be 
some good shots to do. It is also necessary that the King of Naples be certain that his light 
cavalry has defeated the whole country between the Viliya and the Niemen and that it is ensured 
1“ that the enemy has no bridge on the Viliya, 2nd There is neither infantry nor establishment. I 
desire that the geographer-engineer attached to the King not lose a moment in sending you a 
sketch of the whole course of the Viliya and that of the Niemen up to the elbow. Make known to 
the King that, until he finds himself in countries of great plain, he must not be too much 
encumbered with cavalry; that the cuirassiers must be spared; that there is no question but to 
repel the light troops of the enemy and to hear from him in the directions of Olitta and Vilna, and 
to put myself in a position to take the most suitable course of action. Recommend to the King of 
Naples to leave pickets from his vanguard as far as Kovno, so that, independently of the posts, it 
is possible to correspond by orderly officers; which is a sure way” :

and prompt. Recommend to the King of Naples to be sure that Skoruli was well recognized, as 
well as the whole Skorouli road at Jijmory. Send to the king that Marshal Ney, who is at 
Cormilof, receives the order to send strong acknowledgments to Skoroull.

18861. - TO PRINCE OF NEUCHATEL AND WAGRAM, 
MAJOR GENERAL OF THE GREAT ARMY, IN KOVNO. 
Kovno, June 25, 1812. 


Cousin, write to the Duke of Reggio that I suppose that his light cavalry has already 
passed the Viliya at Kovno, that he must send a reconnaissance in the direction of Yanof; that 
three leagues from Kovno there is a junction of the road which goes to Chaty and from there to 
Poneveje and which reaches the Dvina. Poneveje is on the way from Chavli to Vilna. It is 
necessary to illuminate this roll until Jeimy. From Kovno the road goes to the village of Bivili, 
on the Neviaja river. Three leagues farther on is the post office which is in the village of Bobty, 
and six leagues further is Keidany. In Keidanya, Prince Wittgenstein was for a long time, with 
two divisions; it is convenient to know if there is still. It was there that he had to force the light 
cavalry, supported by the cuirassiers, and the Legrand division, which was to march in the 
direction of Bobty; than?’ 


537 


Page 538 


I suppose the river, at this height, is a small thing; that if it is necessary, however, a bridge will 
be made, and then the patrols may proceed to Georgenburg and make its meeting with the 
Grandjean division, that is to say with the 10th corps. From Bobty it will be easy to know if the 
Prince of Wittgenstein is at Keidany, or if he has returned to Rossieny, or whether he has 
marched on Vilkornir to join the Grand Army at Vilna, and finally what direction he has taken. 
My intention is, if he is still in Keidany, to walk to him to dislodge him. Your 2nd division will 
take a position halfway from Rovno to Bobtr, The 3rd will cross the bridge and take position on

of the river in the Niemen. It must be ascertained whether the enemy is in position on the right 
bank of the river. If the enemy were no longer in position on the banks of the river, patrols of 
light cavalry will be carried on Vilki, for the double purpose of having news of the troops which 
the enemy would have on the right bank of the Niemen. , and gather all the boats that we find 
and send them to Kovno.

18862. - TO THE PRINCE OF NEUCHATEL AND WAGRAM, 
MAJOR GENERAL OF THE GREAT ARMY, IN KOVNO. 
Kovno, June 25, 1812. 


Cousin, write to the King of Naples: 

I will send this evening an instruction to your Majesty on the manner in which the 
Emperor intends to make reconnaissance, so as not to compromise any part of his light cavalry. 
His Majesty hopes that the Prince of Eckmiihl will have rallied his army, and that you will have 
rallied your cavalry on your side. You must consult with the Prince of Eckmiihl to choose a good 
position, but which is no more advanced than Jijmory. Before taking a step forward, it is 
necessary that the chessboard is more unraveled. It is especially necessary that one should be 
entirely master of the whole left bank of the Viliya. The viceroy can not be on the line until two 
days. There can be no question now of walking on Vilna; to direct so great a movement, the 
Emperor will go by his person; besides, the left flank must be perfectly assured.

will be responsible for building two raft bridges, one on the Niemen and the other on the Viliya 
opposite Kovno, and two stilt bridges in the same place.

all the obstacles and lend each other mutual aid, so that I can as soon as possible to lift my four

18868. - TO PRINCE OF NEUCHATEL AND WAGRAM, 
MAJOR GENERAL OF THE GREAT ARMY, IN KOVNO. 
Kovno, June 25, 1812. 


The Major-General will order Captain Zakrzewski, attached to the staff of the Duke of 


Danzig, to leave at once with Mr. Heichel to purchase from the vicinity of Kovno the wheat, rye 
or flour that he show.**° 


540 


Page 541 


He will have a detachment of some men at Captain Zakrzewski's disposal to facilitate his 
means of finding wagons and protecting the arrival of these goods. 

The Headquarters Authorizing Officer shall forthwith dispatch a mandate of 3,500 francs 
in favor of Captain Zakrzewski, which sum shall be remitted to him to enable him to pay the 
grain or meal immediately after their departure from the owners. 

Captain Zakrzewski will have the grains and flours taken to the Kovno handling, where 
the quality and quantity will be ascertained, and he will report to the commissioner-in-charge of 
the headquarters of the employment the sum entrusted to him, producing in support of his 
account the receipts of the salesmen.

18869. - TO MAHECHAL DAVOUT, PRINCE OF ECKMUHL, 
COMMANDING THE Ist BODY OF THE GREAT ARMY, IN ROUMCHICHKI. 
Kovno, June 26, 1812, half-past three in the morning. 


Cousin, at the same moment, your aide-de-camp arrives with this student of the 
university. Your convoys must begin to arrive. Gather your troops and rest. Recognize a good 
position in case the enemy walks at you. Press by all means the return of General Friant and that 
of General Compans. Recall all your detachments, in order to assemble your army. It is 
necessary that you stand on guard against an operation that would arrive from Vilkomir on you. 
Besides, I send the Duke of Elchingen with his body to Skoruli, and the Duke of Reggio with his 
own to Yanof. The result of this operation will begin to clarify our position and to make the 
chessboard well known. Until this hour the King of Naples has perhaps been too vile. The army 
is only meeting, and we must not march against an entire army as we march against a beaten 
army. The Duke of Taranto crossed the Tilsit Bridge and walked on Rossieny. The division of 
General Grandjean, who had remained near Georgenburg, seized the city. 

I very much want your geographers to send a sketch with description, which will make 
the country known: whether there are woods, whether they are plains, hills, etc. I can hardly see 
that they are sending none of this. 

NAPOLEON.

18870. - TO THE PRINCE OF NEUCHATEL AND WAGRAM, 
MAJOR GENERAL OF THE GREAT ARMY, IN KOVNO. 
Kovno, June 26, 1812. 


My cousin, order General Eble to begin at midday to raise one of the three boat decks, to 
load it on his bundles and to send him off tomorrow morning, to be returned in the day of the 
27th to the village of Piloni, where he will be bridged for the passage of the Army of Italy. He 
will send with this bridge a superior officer of pontooners who will take the orders of the officer 
commanding the artillery of the 4th corps for the pier of the bridge, which will take place as soon 
as the viceroy will order it and will be able to pass. You will recommend to General Eble to raise 
one of the three bridges, the most difficult passage of which is due to its surroundings. 

Write to the viceroy to let him know that tomorrow morning a boat bridge will leave to 
go to Piloni; that he sends his sailors and his sappers to throw the said bridge, on which he will 
pass with the 4th and the 6th corps and his cavalry. You will let him know that we are occupying 
Jijmory and that we are ten leagues from Vilna. 

NAPOLEON. 

P. S. Write to the viceroy that I would very much like his bridge to be thrown into the 
night of the 27th to the 28th, so that in the day of the 28th he would be in line. 

From the original. Deposit of the war. 


18871. - TO PRINCE OF NEUCHATEL AND WAGRAM, 
MAJOR GENERAL OF THE GREAT ARMY, IN KOVNO. 
Kovno, June 26, 1812. 


Cousin, you realize that there are 520 gendarmes in the army. This number is sufficient, 
but it is poorly distributed; we must leave only five in Berlin, leaving only five in Posen and 
Thorn; do not give it to the crews of the General Staff; I do not see why gendarmes would be 
used to keep luggage; any kind of troops can keep luggage. Give yours your guides, who are 
made for that; that will save you 1 officer and 22 men. Take away those of the King of Naples. 
Give him guides or take light horses: it will save 7. I leave those of the steward, because I guess 
they are not for his luggage, but to execute his orders. Take off the 5 of ”” 


542 


Page 543 


Secretary of State, the two of the Duke of Treviso and the Duke of Danzig, those of inspectors to 
the journals, those who are distributed to the various safeguards. So there are many gendarmes 
who become available again. Men are probably needed for the services they were responsible 
for; but take in the company of guides, which can be increased, also take in the cavalry. A 
gendarme is not a man on horseback; it is an agent who must be placed in every post, because 
this service is the most important, who must be in charge of the police on the rear of the army 
and must not be employed either in safeguard or for escorts, nor to keep any kind of baggage. I 
do not oppose the request of a squadron of cavalry until the arrival of the regiment of Baden, 
which you may employ in the service of the staff. All the army corps have too much 
gendarmerie; we use it, not for the police, but for the luggage escort, and that's not their job. 
Present me a draft regulation on this subject; it is not that I find that the service they are doing is 
not to be done, but I think this service should not be done by them. By making these reforms in 
the different corps, you can very well give each corps only 40 gendarmes. I shall have no 
objection to authorizing every general and every individual entitled to escort his baggage to raise 
a certain number of Poles for this service. Meanwhile, take cavalry: 2 or 300 men of cavalry 
more or less are nothing; 200 more gendarmes ensure the tranquility of the army and good order. 

NAPOLEON. 

From the original. Deposit of the war.

My Cousin, you will find attached the state of the convoys which left on the 25th for 
Tilsit. Send an officer to meet them. Write to General Bachelu at Georgenburg to protect the

unload these convoys at Tilsit; make it feel absurd, and let your officer take care of them 
without

delay; let him see the Prussian officers who will offer escorts for hauling.

18873. - TO THE PRINCE OF NEUCHATEL AND WAGRAM, 
MAJOR GENERAL OF THE GREAT ARMY, IN KOVNO. 
Kovno, June 26, 1812. 


Cousin, write to the Duke of Elchingen that our outposts are five leagues from Vilna, that 
Yevé is occupied by our troops, that it appears that General Baggovoute has gone from Vanof to 
Tchabiehki, where he has passed the Viliya, and that it is directed by Mousniki, Ghedroitsky, 
Koltyniany and Vidzy; that I do not know what Russian General Wittgenstein will have done, 
but that he was at Keidany on the 25th; that it appears that General Wittgenstein commands the 
Ist corps of the right, that General Baggovoute commands the 2nd, and General Toutchkof the 
3rd; that each of these corps appears to be two strong divisions of 20,000 men; that it is supposed 
that from Troki the bulk of the army goes to Vilna and from Vilna to Sventsiany; that Vanof is 
evacuated, as I suppose. I want him to start a vanguard today as soon as he can on Yeguzhin, and 
tomorrow morning he will walk so as to make a great day and get as close as possible, for 
example, to the village of Palki, in the direction of Vilna; that [am going to Jijmory tonight; that 
on the 27th we could enter Vilna. 

Write to the Duke of Remlio and the Duke of Taranto to communicate to them the same 
details on the right of the enemy and on our respective positions. Make known to the Duke of 
Reggio that it is necessary that he march tomorrow on Jeirny, to attack Wittgenstein, or at least 
to know the movement he makes and to clear the Niemen entirely. Write to the Duke of Taranto 
that the Duke of Reggio arrived today at Yanof and marches on Jeymy and Chaly; that he will 
attack Wittgenstein, unless he re-reads himself on Chavli, that I hope that the Duke of Taranto 
will go to Rossieny, leaving infantry posts on the left bank of the Niemen, to be perfectly sure of 
navigation. 

NAPOLEON. 


From the original. Deposit of the war.°“*

18874. - TO THE PRINCE OF NEUCHATEL AND WAGRAM, 
MAJOR GENERAL OF THE GREAT ARMY, IN VILNA. 
Vilna, June 29, 1812. 


Cousin, give orders to the Prince of Eckmihl that Friant's division be at the disposal of 
the King of Naples, and that the Gudin division should pass the Viliya bridge at nine o'clock in 
the morning, to be at the disposal of the King; that Morand's division leaves at three o'clock in 
the morning, and goes on to follow Mikhalichki; it will be illuminated by the Polish Light 
Cavalry Brigade, which, for this purpose, will join this route to Lovarichki, speaking of the 
position at which it is at one o'clock in the morning. The Compans division will also leave at 
three o'clock in the morning to go to Ochmiana; he will have with him the Pajol brigade, and a 
regiment of this division will meet on Soletchniki and be under the orders of General 
Bordesoulle. The prince of Eckmiihl will go to Mikhalichki himself and lead with him the 
division Valencia. Order General Nansouty to leave with the Saint-Germain division to support 
the Bruyere division and to follow the enemy on Korkojichki, taking the orders of the King of 
Naples, who will maneuver on the right bank, and concert with the Prince of Eckmiihl, who goes 
on Mikhalichki. 

Order the King of Naples to leave with the corps of Montbrun, the corps of Nansouty, the 
division Saint-Germain on the left bank, the divisions Eriant and Gudill, and to drive the enemy 
of Niementchine and to follow him in his retreat; to bind himself with the Duke of Elchingen, 
who is to be at Mieishagola this evening, and to direct him in the same direction on the enemy, 
charging him to send strong acknowledgments on Vilkomir to find out what exists there. 

Order the Duke of Elchingen to support the King of Naples and send an acknowledgment 
to Vilkomir; Let him know that the Duke of Reggio is going to Chaly to attack General 
Wittgenstein. 

At last you will order the King of Naples to have cavalry posts every three leagues, in 
order to correspond easily; you will give the same order to General Nansouty and to Prince 
Eckmihl. 

Recommend to the commanders of these three columns to correspond frequently with 
you, so that I can make arrangements to support them. It would also be necessary that, in each of 
these three directions, three companies of voltigeurs leave as soon as possible to support the 
cavalry. Unless we had a 


545 


Page 546 


positive knowledge of the progress of the enemy, and that we do not know what we are doing, 
we should not tire the troops too much. It is necessary to enlighten the three roads, not only by 
parties, but also by locals. 
NAPOLEON. 
From the original. Deposit of the war. 


18875. - TO JEROME NAPOLEON, KING OF WESTPHALIA, 
COMMANDING THE 5th, 7th AND 8th CORPS OF THE GREAT ARMY, IN GRODNO. 
Vilna, June 29, 1812. 


Sire, the Emperor has charged me to inform your Majesty that we entered yesterday at 
Vilna, which the enemy has evacuated after having burned the bridge and immense stores. The 
Emperor assumes that your Majesty is at this moment in Grodno. Bagration's corps is in 
Ochmiaua. Your Majesty must therefore go with his army corps on Ochmiaua. Your Majesty 
will give our news to the Prince of Schwavzenberg. It results from intercepted couriers that there 
are no more troops in Volhynia. If this is true and there are no more forces on this side, Prince 
Schwarzenberg must maneuver in the direction of Brzesc to Slonime. 

By order of the Emperor, 
ALEXANDRE, Prince of Neuchearel and Wagram. 
From the Memoirs of King Jerome. 


18876. - TO THE PRINCE OF NEUCHATEL AND WAGRAM, 
MAJOR GENERAL OF THE GREAT ARMY, IN VILNA 
Vilna, June 30, 1812. 


Cousin, send orders to General Eble to go to Vilna with all his crews. He will raise the 
bridge which serves at this moment to the Viceroy, as soon as he has passed. I need to have a 
first detachment of the deck crew here, and then the whole thing. The service of Kovno will be 
done by a bridge on stilts on the Niemen, and by a raft bridge on the Viliya. In Vilna the service 
will be done by a bridge on stilts and by the rafts which are there. Give the order to the enginner 
to bring his park to Vilna, leaving at most two companies of sappers in Kovno and the necessary 
officers to the works. A company of sappers and the necessary officers will also be left in Vilna; 
the Danube battalion and the sailors of the Guard will go to Vilna. There will remain in Kovno 
an officer and fifty sailors of the 4th crew; give order that two companies” 


546 


Page 547 


of the Scheldt battalion go to Kovno. Thus the battalion of the Scheldt will have a company at 
Danzig, one at Koenigsberg, and two at Kovno. The harnessed tools and a company of workers 
will go to Vilna. I approve of General Chasseloup's idea, and grant to the engineers the battalion 
of the Danube and two companies of the battalion of the Scheldt. As for the 4th crew of sailors, 
he has his particular service; it will help engineering, pontoons and navigation. Ask the engineer 
general when the park sets off for Vilna. Order the general of artillery to bring two millions of 
cartridges and twenty thousand guns to Vilna; all this can come by water, the Niemen is entirely 
free. Recommend General Chasseloup to give me every eight days an exact report on the work of 
Kovno and Vilna. 

NAPOLEON. 
From the original. Deposit of the war. 


18877. - TO THE PRINCE OF NEUCHATEL AND WAGRAM, 
MAJOR GENERAL OF THE GREAT ARMY, IN VILNA, 
Vilna, June 30, 1812. 


Cousin, send to the Duke of Elchingen, that I thought he would be at Mieichagola 
yesterday; that it is indispensable that he should proceed without delay, and that he should make 
strong admissions on Vilkomir; that his order was to know what had happened to Mousniki; that 
I was hoping that by the 28th he would have made this reconnaissance, which would have given 
him information on the direction of Baggovoute; that Wittgenstein was in Vilkomir on the 27th; 
that he had left no one to Keidany; that the Duke of Reggio is much stronger than Wittgenstein; 
that it was only by a change of direction in the march of Baggovoute that the Duke of Reggio 
could have had to deal with a large part; that, consequently, I had ordered the Duke of Elchingen 
to ascertain the course of Baggovoute, and that it is with difficulty that I see that he has not done 
so; that I have just received news of the Duke of Reggio, who from Cat went there on Vilkomir, 
where he found the 5th and 14th divisions composing the corps of Wittgenstein, with Ouvarof 
and the Grand Duke Constantine, that all this had to make about 16,000 men; that he pushed 
them hard, took them off the bridge of Vilkornir, and made 500 prisoners; that this enemy corps 
retreats to Dinabourg; that, consequently, I order the King of Naples, who marches with three 
divisions of infantry and five of cavalry, to direct his course more openly to Sventsiany, and 
which I desire him to occupy without delay.>”” 


547 


Page 548 


Mieichagola and from there goes on Ghedroitsy, where he will communicate with the Duke of 
Reggio, and from where he can march on Vilkomir or Sventsiany, according to the 
circumstances; that it will be convenient that, as soon as Sventsiany is occupied by our troops, he 
will rise, in column, so as to be at the same height and in communication; that the Prince of 
Eckmiithl is on his side with two divisions against several enemy columns, encamped on the side 
of Ochmiana; that three divisions of Bagration were forced to march on Vilna, that they were 
already two marches the day after our entry into Vilna; let them go against them and pursue 
them; that many stores and officers are taken every day, that we are already at the 5th and 6th 
dispatch from Russia, and addressed to the general-in-chief who was here; that the loss of the 
stores they have already burned in the first, second and third line is estimated at 15 to 20 
millions; that, according to all the information taken, the enemy had on the right, from the 
marshes of Pinsk, four corps d'armee, each of two divisions, namely: Ist the corps of 
Wittgenstein, composed of the 5th and 14th divisions forming 12,000 men (the Duke of Reggio 
has more than 30,000); 2nd the corps of Baggovoure, composed of the 4th and 17th divisions, 
12,000 men; 3rd the corps of Chouvalof, composed of the Ist division of grenadiers and the 3rd 
division, 12,000 men, 4th finally of the corps of Toutchkof composed of the 7th and 11th 
divisions, 12,000 men, that these eight divisions do not make 48,000 men of the infantry, that the 
five sixths are recruits, that, if we add 10,000 men of the imperial guard, we see that all the 
infantry which was here in the north barely amount to 60,000 men; with the artillery and the 
cavalry, etc., this does not form an army of 80,000 men, which we know positively that the 
Russian divisions are composed, namely: the great of six regiments, the averages of five, some of 
four, but to calculate more than less they are all six, one regiment has only two battalions, one 
battalion only four, and therefore There are not 1,000 men per regiment. 

Reiterate the order to the Duke of Elchingen to communicate with the Duke of Reggio, 
and if he is opposite Baggovoute, who does not have 14,000 men, let him attack him vigorously. 

NAPOLEON.

18878. - TO THE PRINCE OF NEUCHATEL AND WAGRAM, 
MAJOR GENERAL OF THE GREAT ARMY, IN VILNA 
Vilna, June 30, 1812. 


Cousin, tell the Duke of Reagio that I am satisfied with the conduct he has held and the 
manner in which he has maneuvered. Let him know the direction taken by the King of Naples 
and that of the Duke of Elchingen, as well as the actual composition of the Russian army, as I put 
it in the dispatch which I have told you to send to the Duke of Elchingen. Tell him that General 
Wittgenstein had before him only 15,000 men, including the Knights-Guards; that I have the 
state of situation of this corps, which has been intercepted, and that independently all the 
elements that I have lead to this result. Recommend him not to tire his troops, to rally them, to 
try to organize the subsistence and to establish a good police. Tell him that I suppose that, by 
means of Corbineau's brigade, he has news of the Marshal Duke of Taranto, who on his side 
must give him his. Also let him know that the immense stores that the enemy had here were 
burned. Make known to the Duke of Taranto that he has no one left before him, Wittgenstein 
retiring on Dinabourg; ask him to occupy Poneueje, Chavli, and Telchi, and to spare the 
inhabitants of the country, who are for us. Tell him that it would not be impossible for him to 
receive the order to march on Mitau, since it appears that the whole hostile army is reading over 
Dinahonrg and Disna. He must put the place of Memel in very good condition. I look forward to 
seeing, from the plans and reports of the engineers, what it is that places and what can be 
expected. This point put in state, one could disembark there the crew of siege for the siege of 
Riga. Recommend to the Duke of Taranto to correspond with the Duke of Reggio by his outposts 
and also by Kovno. Tell him that we are still waiting impatiently for Tilsit's convoys. 

NAPOLEON. 

According to the original. Deposit of the war.
